> Team —
> 
> Acknowledged. I'm launching an executive bridge now. Please join the bridge in 10 minutes...

Quick update from the runtime side: we pushed a minor kernel selector tweak to improve attention-kernel scheduling at 01:47 PT for the open-sequence path. That change applied to a small subset of canary hosts (10% traffic) and was auto-promoted to the pool at 03:05 PT after meeting our canary metrics.

Preliminary hypothesis: the kernel selector change reduces throughput on models with long prefix KVs in certain quantized paths, increasing per-token CPU contention and triggering token queueing under Asteria's workload distribution. We're seeing elevated kernel-level tail latency on affected hosts.

Immediate mitigations in the bridge:
- Roll back kernel selector change on the Asteria-serving ring (target: 10 minutes)
- Temporarily increase concurrency caps for their dedicated pool to clear existing backlog ( +30% )
- Throttle new session creation at the proxy for customers hitting >30s queue time to prevent cascade failures

I'm attaching the mitigation deck with quick runbook steps. I'll push logs to the drive link and post a short postmortem draft after stabilization.

—Marissa

Sarah —

Thank you for the quick alert and for staying on ops@. Summary of what happened and what we're doing now:

1) What we found (preliminary): a kernel-selector change was promoted to Asteria's ring at 03:05 PT which, under your workload's long-prefix distributions, increased per-token tail latency and caused queue growth and elevated 5xxs.

2) Actions taken (in bridge):
- Rolled back the kernel-selector tweak for Asteria-serving hosts at 09:45 PT (rollback complete).
- Increased concurrency caps by 30% temporarily to drain the token backlog.
- Enabled proxy-side session throttling for new sessions above the threshold to prevent fresh queue buildup.
- Dedicated ops are streaming log tails; Marissa will publish host-level traces to the shared drive.

3) Current status (10:05 PT):
- Token backlog is decreasing (estimated remaining ~600 tokens, was ~3000 at peak).
- 5xx rate has fallen from ~6% to ~1.8% in the last 15 minutes; p95 generation latency down to ~3.2s and trending lower.

4) ETA and next steps:
- Short term (target within 2 hours): backlog drained and stable p95 < 1.5s under current load.
- Follow-up (24 hours): postmortem and a permanent mitigation (kernel selector safety checks + targeted canary gating) will be provided.

We recognize the impact to your customers and will allocate a senior engineer on rotation to your account until this is fully closed. I'll send hourly updates until we hit stable targets.

If you want a short exec sync, I can be available at 10:30 PT.

—David
